findings.claim: The fallback archives whatever active memory holds the derived key `<key>/part-i`, so an unrelated memory can be archived when the moved part's title was edited. The moved part is then not recognised because its title no longer ends ` (part i/oldParts)`. The fallback runs and archives the unrelated holder of `<key>/part-i`, while the moved part stays active. The intent says the derived key holds the part 'regardless of title', so this is the accepted tradeoff, but nothing tests or documents it.
evidence: The first UPDATE (lines 162-168) needs a title match. When the title was edited it affects 0 rows, and the second UPDATE (lines 178-183) filters only on `topic_key=?` and status. The importer (import.go:195-227) moves a part to `~N` and gives the freed key to another memory. The new test covers only the non-moved edited-title case. I did not run the tests.

findings.claim: The RowsAffected handling is awkward. `err != nil || n > 0` followed by a nested `if err != nil` hides the error return inside the success branch, and `err` is shadowed.
evidence: Lines 172-177. Clearer form: `n, err := moved.RowsAffected(); if err != nil { return ... }; if n > 0 { continue }`.

findings.claim: The new test covers only the edited-title, un-moved case. No test covers the F1 edge, an edited moved part together with an unrelated holder at the derived key, which would pin the chosen behaviour.
evidence: The diff adds one test. It renames the part at `doc/part-3` and re-saves the document short. It asserts the part is archived and nothing else.
